basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE BANGSAMORO ELECTORAL CODE OF BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Provides for the Bangsamoro Electoral Code of BARMM.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Governs the Sept 14, 2026 first parliamentary elections; amended by BAA 87 (NOTA removal) and BAA 88.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Provides for the Bangsamoro Electoral Code of BARMM.
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Ratified 2023-03-08; effectivity per the Act's final section (typically 15 days after Official Gazette publication).

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: The Electoral Code is the rulebook for the first-ever Bangsamoro Parliament elections on September 14, 2026: how you vote, what a party needs to run, how the 80 seats (district, party, and sectoral) are filled. It is the single law that most directly turns residents into voters of their own regional government.
in_practice: Creates the regional party system - you will vote for parties and district representatives, not just personalities
Sets registration, campaign, and canvassing rules jointly implemented with COMELEC
Already amended twice (BAA 87 removed the 'None of the Above' ballot option; BAA 88 made further refinements) - check the amended text

for_specific_groups.First-time voters: Register with COMELEC; your ballot will look different from national elections
for_specific_groups.Aspiring candidates & parties: Accreditation and eligibility rules are here
for_specific_groups.Women & sectoral groups: Reserved sectoral seats and party rules affect representation

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All of BARMM unless the title names a specific place
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Laws take effect shortly after publication, but felt impact follows budgets, IRRs, and agency rollout - typically months, not days
what_you_can_do: Ask your municipal/barangay office or the implementing ministry how and when it will roll out where you live
Read the full text (PDF) on the Parliament's website or the Official Gazette of the Bangsamoro - the final sections say when it takes effect and who must act
If it isn't being implemented, raise it with your Member of Parliament or through the ministry's public assistance desk
watch_out_for: Already amended by BAA 87, 88 - read the consolidated text

key_terms_explained.BAA: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act - a regional law passed by the Bangsamoro Parliament, applying inside BARMM alongside national laws.
key_terms_explained.IRR: Implementing Rules and Regulations - the ministry-issued 'how-to' that turns a law's text into procedures; many laws only bite once the IRR is out.
key_terms_explained.GAA: General Appropriations Act - the annual budget law deciding how much each ministry and program gets.

benefits.headline: The machinery of your first real regional vote.

direct_benefits.benefit: The right to elect the Bangsamoro Parliament - district, party, and sectoral seats
Rules that let regional parties and sectoral groups compete, not just national machines

indirect_benefits: Peace dividend: ballots replacing bullets as the route to power
limitations: Amended by BAA 87 (no NOTA) and BAA 88 - read the consolidated text
